correctness.rationale: The graph edge-pair trichotomy has exact weights (1,n-2,(p-1)(q-1))/pq and intrinsic conditional distances |U-V|, U+V and 2-|U-V|. Their elementary triangular distributions give the claimed piecewise CDF and integrate to mu=5/3-2n/(3P), m2=17/6-(5n-2)/(3P). Delta=6m2+8-15mu=4/P recovers P, then n, hence unordered (p,q). For fixed n the CDF is C+(A+(n-2)B-(n-1)C)/P with strictly positive numerator for every 0<r<2; as p balances P increases. Uniform vertex sampling instead has CDF (n+2P)/n^2 on 1<=r<2, proving a strict reversal. The diameter tail linear/quadratic phase follows directly from the upper CDF. Star and single-edge boundary cases are included.

originality.rationale: Important prior overlap: published November 1 Continuous two-point geodesic tomography of complete bipartite metric graphs already gives the identical FULL density, the mean, and parameter recovery using the near-zero density. Thus neither the distance law nor identification from a full law is novel, and the two-moment inverse is a simple further algebraic consequence of that already known density. The surviving, separately assessable assertion is strict first-order stochastic monotonicity under balancing of the continuous arclength law and its opposite direction under vertex-uniform sampling, including all thresholds and boundary cases. Those contrasting orders are not stated in the inspected earlier full theorem. Value rests on this substantive sampling-measure reversal, not on repackaging the known law.
residual_risks: The reversal is an elementary monotonicity corollary of an already-published exact density; future originality/value assessment may regard that consequence as too routine. This uncertainty is explicitly preserved rather than claiming the density as new.

value.rationale: The same fixed family of metric graphs reverses the direction of every strictly increasing distance functional when one changes between two canonical sampling measures. This exact universal first-order stochastic phenomenon, including the unique extremal star and balanced cases and the contrasting diameter-tail cycle threshold, is an interpretable natural geometric effect beyond merely reprinting an exact probability density. The two-moment algebra is not independently presented as a major new theorem.
